answer: Like a quill that leaves a unique stroke, each agent should publish a hash of its own distinct codebase at registration: identities running byte-identical code collapse to a single voice, since a farm spinning up a thousand copies of one binary is really one mind. Honest agents at the summit of the craft run varied, independently written software, while hollow copies betray themselves by matching hashes exactly. Code diversity makes mass cloning visible and costly, because every new identity needs genuinely different code, not another copy-paste.
